tldr: InfiGUI-R1 introduces the Actor2Reasoner framework, a two-stage training approach that transforms MLLM-based GUI agents from reactive actors into deliberative reasoners using spatial reasoning distillation and reinforcement learning with sub-goal guidance and error recovery.
contributions: Proposes the Actor2Reasoner framework, a novel two-stage training methodology to transform MLLM-based GUI agents from Reactive Actors into Deliberative Reasoners

Introduces three technical innovations: Spatial Reasoning Distillation for cross-modal reasoning, Sub-goal Guidance for planning, and Error Recovery Scenario Construction for reflective self-correction
Develops InfiGUI-R1-3B, an MLLM-based GUI agent demonstrating state-of-the-art performance
methods: The Actor2Reasoner framework has two stages. Stage 1 (Reasoning Injection) identifies reasoning bottleneck samples where the base MLLM fails without sub-goals but succeeds with them, then uses a teacher model to generate explicit spatial reasoning trajectories from accessibility tree information, followed by supervised fine-tuning to establish a Perception→Reasoning→Action pattern. Stage 2 (Deliberation Enhancement) applies REINFORCE Leave-One-Out reinforcement learning with rule-based rewards, incorporating sub-goal guidance (rewarding accurate intermediate sub-goal generation) and error recovery scenario construction (creating failure-and-recovery training scenarios) to enhance planning and self-correction capabilities.
results: InfiGUI-R1-3B achieves 87.5% average accuracy on ScreenSpot (cross-platform GUI grounding benchmark) and a 71.1% success rate on AndroidControl-High (long-horizon task execution benchmark), performing competitively against previous agents including those with significantly larger parameters.
limitations: The paper does not explicitly state limitations; however, the framework relies on a powerful teacher model (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct) for distillation, and the RL stage requires carefully constructed reward functions and error recovery scenarios that may be challenging to generalize across all GUI environments.
